en: Hi, everyone.

en: We're going to start right on time because I'm going to speak basically at 2x.
zh: 我们要准时开始,因为我基本上要以 2 倍速来讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sorry I have a lot of content.
zh: 很抱歉,我有很多内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm trying to get you out here on time.
zh: 我想让你们能准时离开这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with a quick raise of hands.
zh: 我想先快速举一下手。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how many of you have built your own agents or are currently building your own agents?
zh: 那么你们中有多少人构建了自己的智能体,或者正在构建自己的智能体?

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfectly.
zh: 完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're the right audience for this.
zh: 你们是本次演讲的合适受众。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over the next 20 minutes, I want to talk to you about a couple of different things that we're doing in the Codex harness that hopefully you can learn to apply to your own use cases or even just use the Codex harness with this in
zh: 在接下来的 20 分钟里,我想和你们谈谈我们在 Codex harness 中正在做的几件事,希望你们能学会将其应用到你们自己的用例中,或者甚至直接将 Codex harness 用在

speaker: Unknown
en: In your own projects, or at bare minimum, learn what happens when you actually use Codex.
zh: 你们自己的项目中,或者至少,了解一下当你实际使用 Codex 时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Since we're at iEngineer World's Fair and we're actually on an agentic engineering track, I'm gonna stop bothering you with how does an agent work?
zh: 既然我们在 iEngineer World's Fair 并且实际上是在智能体工程专场,我就不再打扰你们,不再去讲智能体是如何工作的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is an agent?
zh: 什么是智能体?

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead, I want to talk a bit more specifically about some key features that we have in the agent that I think are particularly interesting and are challenges you have to solve.
zh: 相反,我想更具体地谈谈我们在智能体中的一些我认为特别有趣的关键特性,也是你们必须解决的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let's cover it from the lens of what actually happens when you send off a message.
zh: 让我们从当你发送一条消息时实际发生了什么这个角度来涵盖它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, a quick reminder, if you're unaware, the Codex harness and everything I'm showing you is actually open source.
zh: 另外,快速提醒一下,如果你不知道,Codex harness 以及我向你展示的所有内容实际上是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Apache 2 license, and the harness is written in Rust, so feel free to either learn from it, ask Codex deeper questions about what I'm covering, or fork it and make it your own.
zh: 它是 Apache 2 许可证,harness 是用 Rust 编写的,所以请随时从中学习,向 Codex 提出关于我所讲内容的更深层问题,或者分叉它并把它变成你自己的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also disclaimer before we dive deep into it, this is a current state of affairs, like things change so quickly.
zh: 在我们深入探讨之前的免责声明,这是当前的状况,事情变化得很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can always refer back to asking Codex what the current state is, but especially with new model releases, we often release new APIs and change sort of how the harness works.
zh: 你总是可以回过头来询问 Codex 目前的状态是什么,但特别是随着新模型的发布,我们经常发布新的 API 并稍微改变 harness 的工作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So feel free to follow along as new models come out.
zh: 所以请随时关注新模型的发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we want to talk about how the Codex agent works, we first need to talk about what actually happens when you send off your message.
zh: 如果我们要谈论 Codex 智能体是如何工作的,我们首先需要谈谈当你发送消息时实际发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Namely, there's two protocols that are involved with the Codex agent.
zh: 具体来说,涉及 Codex 智能体的有两个协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is what happens when you send it off in the UI and it goes to the harness.
zh: 第一个是当你在 UI 中发送它并且它进入 harness 时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call that the app server.
zh: 我们称之为应用服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked about that yesterday, so we're not going to spend too much time about it.
zh: 我昨天讲过那个,所以我们不会花太多时间讲它。

speaker: Unknown
en: There will be a talk online that you can follow along.
zh: 会有一个在线讲座,你可以跟随学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second part is the responses API, which handles the communication between the harness and the inference.
zh: 第二部分是 responses API,它处理 harness 和推理之间的通信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both of these, though, are designed for an open ecosystem, meaning if you're building your own UI, you're building your own agent interface, you can actually build on top of the Codex harness using the app server protocol.
zh: 不过,这两个都是为了一个开放的生态系统设计的,这意味着如果你正在构建自己的 UI,你正在构建自己的智能体接口,你实际上可以使用应用服务器协议在 Codex harness 之上构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use that same app server to power the Codex app, so it has really all of that functionality that you might expect from Codex, as well as we have a lot of third-party community projects that build on top of it, including Theos T3 Code or RemoteX, for example.
zh: 我们使用同样的应用服务器来驱动 Codex 应用,所以它实际上具有你可能期望从 Codex 获得的所有功能,以及我们有很多第三方社区项目在上面构建,包括 Theos T3 Code 或 RemoteX,例如。

speaker: Unknown
en: I even used that same app server to put Codex into Claude Code.
zh: 我甚至使用同样的应用服务器将 Codex 放入了 Claude Code。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're a Claude Code user and you want to leverage Codex, you can use that plugin.
zh: 所以如果你是 Claude Code 用户并且你想利用 Codex,你可以使用那个插件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you joined my talk yesterday, you saw me using that same protocol to actually put Codex into Doom, which was a fun adventure as well.
zh: 如果你参加了我昨天的讲座,你看到我使用同样的协议实际上将 Codex 放入了 Doom,那也是一次有趣的冒险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mentioned the other part is the responses API.
zh: 我提到的另一部分是 responses API。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the response API was released last year as a rethinking of the chat completions API in a more agentic world, meaning we redesigned slightly the structure, but more importantly, we added a lot of building capabilities that are important for agents like web search, image gen, or other more complex capabilities that you will see as part of this talk.
zh: responses API 去年作为聊天完成 API 的重新思考而发布,以适应更智能化的世界,这意味着我们稍微重新设计了结构,但更重要的是,我们添加了很多对智能体很重要的构建能力,比如网络搜索、图像生成,或者你将作为本次演讲的一部分看到的其他更复杂的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also want to make sure that this is like an open ecosystem.
zh: 我们还想确保这是一个开放的生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we worked with a lot of partners, including Llama, LM Studio, NVIDIA, and others to codify an open responses schema and have a governance body for that so that other companies and platforms can actually build on that same responses API.
zh: 所以我们与许多合作伙伴合作,包括 Llama、LM Studio、NVIDIA 和其他公司,以制定一个开放的 responses 架构并为此设立一个管理机构,以便其他公司和平台实际上可以在同一个 responses API 上构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can use any responses API compatible model provider and actually plug it into the Codex harness.
zh: 你可以使用任何与 responses API 兼容的模型提供商,并实际将其插入 Codex harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's an overview of how these protocols work.
zh: 这就是这些协议如何工作的概述。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going from the UI to the harness with the app server protocol, and then from the harness to the LM inference using responses.
zh: 我们通过应用服务器协议从 UI 到 harness,然后通过 responses 从 harness 到 LM 推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what happens in the actual harness?
zh: 但在实际的 harness 中会发生什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: The first step, and arguably one of the most important ones, is context construction.
zh: 第一步,可以说也是最重要的一步,是上下文构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And during that, we care about three things quite a lot.
zh: 在此期间,我们非常关心三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is size.
zh: 第一个是大小。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to make sure that we don't blast through your token budgets and throw in a bunch of unnecessary content.
zh: 我们要确保我们不会耗尽你的 token 预算,也不会扔进一堆不必要的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also, the more context you have in your context, the higher it is that you have contradicting information, and it causes confusion for the model.
zh: 但同样,你的上下文中的上下文越多,你拥有相互矛盾的信息的可能性就越高,这会导致模型产生困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other part is flexibility.
zh: 另一部分是灵活性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to make sure that regardless of many or how little skills you're using, you have a great experience, regardless of how many plugins and MCPs you install.
zh: 我们要确保无论你使用多少技能,或者很少的技能,你都有很好的体验,无论你安装了多少插件和 MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, we want to make sure that things are performant and we know you're cost sensitive, so cacheability is important as well.
zh: 当然,我们要确保事情是高性能的,我们知道你对成本敏感,所以可缓存性也很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: To show you this and a couple of other things, I actually built this little nano codex here, which functions the same way.
zh: 为了向你展示这一点以及其他几件事,我实际上在这里构建了这个小小的 nano codex,它的功能是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's built using the same code that is on the public repo, just turned into TypeScript.
zh: 它是使用公共代码库上的相同代码构建的,只是转换成了 TypeScript。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we can see here, when we send off a message, we have a couple of different parts of the actual context that gets assembled.
zh: 但我们可以在这里看到,当我们发送一条消息时,我们有几个不同的实际上下文部分被组装在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of these are fairly standard and predictable, like the model instructions.
zh: 其中一些是相当标准和可预测的,比如模型指令。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, these are open source if you actually want to read them.
zh: 再说一次,如果你真的想阅读它们,这些都是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But these are fairly structured and don't really change in size or mess around with cacheability.
zh: 但这些是相当结构化的,并且在大小上不会真正改变,也不会干扰可缓存性。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are some parts that are harder to predict.
zh: 但有些部分更难预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: Namely, for example, how many skills do you have available?
zh: 即,例如,你有多少可用的技能?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or the tool registry, where, especially if you install MCPs, for example, you might have additional context that is growing as you're installing more MCPs.
zh: 或者是工具注册表,在这里,特别是如果你安装 MCPs,例如,你可能有额外的上下文,随着你安装更多的 MCPs 而增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: For that reason, we do two things to maintain costs.
zh: 因此,我们做两件事来维持成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is, or the size of the context, the first one is having deferred tools.
zh: 第一件事是,或者上下文的大小,第一件事是拥有延迟工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're marking some of these tools as deferred, and that means that they're not added directly to the context window, but instead are available through tool search later on.
zh: 所以我们将其中一些工具标记为延迟的,这意味着它们没有直接添加到上下文窗口,而是通过稍后的工具搜索可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other part is that for available skills, we actually cap the available skills list at 2% of your maximum context window.
zh: 然后另一部分是,对于可用的技能,我们实际上将可用技能列表上限设为你最大上下文窗口的 2%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that if it gets longer, we're reducing slowly the amount of description that we're putting in there.
zh: 这意味着如果它变长,我们正在缓慢减少我们在那里放入的描述的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tool search specifically is actually something that is available in the responses API.
zh: 工具搜索特别地,实际上是在 responses API 中可用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even if you're building your own harness, you can leverage this.
zh: 所以即使你正在构建你自己的挽具,你可以利用这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Since GPT 5.4, you can mark any tool as deferred loading.
zh: 自从 GPT 5.4 以来,你可以将任何工具标记为延迟加载。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that these tools are only available if you're using tool search.
zh: 这意味着这些工具只有在你使用工具搜索时才可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can give the model either our built-in tool search tool or implement your own if you feel like you can better do that discovery yourself.
zh: 然后你可以给模型我们要么内置的工具搜索工具,或者实现你自己的,如果你觉得你可以自己做那个发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great, we talked about how we're building the context, but an agent really only becomes an agent if it performs actions.
zh: 很棒,我们谈论了我们正在如何构建上下文,但智能体真的只有在它执行动作时才成为智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's three common actions I wanted to talk about.
zh: 我想谈论三个常见的动作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is async actions, things that are happening while the agent has to continue to do work, computer use, and then the file system.
zh: 第一个是异步动作,正在发生的事情,而智能体必须继续工作,计算机使用,然后是文件系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: For async actions, a good example is subagents where we want to be able to delegate tasks off and then have the main agent continue to do work if necessary.
zh: 对于异步动作,一个很好的例子是子智能体,我们希望能够将任务委托出去,然后让主智能体如果必要继续工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that works in practice is that we give the agent a spawn agent tool, which then allows the agent to create new agent instances and then use a send input tool to either send new content to those newly created agents, wait for an agent, or shut it back down.
zh: 这在实践中工作的方式是,我们给智能体一个孵化智能体工具,然后允许智能体创建新的智能体实例,然后使用一个发送输入工具来要么向那些新创建的智能体发送新内容,等待一个智能体,或将其关闭。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use that same concept actually for background terminals as well.
zh: 我们实际上为后台终端也使用相同的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the Codex agent has a tool to spin up a new background terminal and then continuously interact with it by sending new data through standard in to that new agent or wait for a specific amount of time for that agent to finish a task.
zh: 所以 Codex 智能体有一个工具来启动一个新的后台终端,然后通过向那个新智能体发送标准输入的新数据或等待特定时间让那个智能体完成任务来持续与它交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: Computer use is an interesting one because we actually introduced computer use in the responses API last year and it was fairly limited.
zh: 计算机使用是一个有趣的,因为我们实际上去年在 responses API 中引入了计算机使用,并且它是相当有限的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It only allowed you to do one action at a time and you had to basically declare that you wanted it to do computer use and from there you were up to actually implementing specifically the type of actions that were exposed to that tool.
zh: 它一次只允许你做一个动作,你必须基本上声明你想要它做计算机使用,从那里你实际上要实现专门暴露给该工具的动作类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was great in terms of that point in the journey of building agents, but since then we've evolved it, and the recent models and the recent API shapes allow you to use code execution instead to actually do computer use, which means that the agent can script its own interactions with whatever computer implementation you want to have.
zh: 这在构建智能体旅程的那一点上很棒,但自那时起我们进化了它,最近的模型和最近的 API 形状允许你使用代码执行来做计算机使用,这意味着智能体可以编写它与任何你想要的计算机实现的交互脚本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can choose the language, like JavaScript or Python, and you have a much more flexible harness.
zh: 你可以选择语言,比如 JavaScript 或 Python,并且你有一个更灵活的挽具。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, that's what we use for browser use.
zh: 事实上,这就是我们用于浏览器使用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens when Codex uses browser use is it actually interacts with a persistent node REPL that gets persisted throughout the turns.
zh: 所以当 Codex 使用浏览器使用时发生的是,它实际上与一个持久化的节点 REPL 交互,它贯穿于轮次之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it writes JavaScript, essentially play-write code, to interact with that browser instance in the node REPL.
zh: 然后它编写 JavaScript,本质上剧本写作代码,来在节点 REPL 中与那个浏览器实例交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's an example where on the right side we have a Chromium browser and the first time it writes some code to get the overall status and pulls up the right tab.
zh: 所以这里有一个例子,在右侧我们有一个 Chromium 浏览器,第一次它编写一些代码来获取整体状态并拉起正确的标签页。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on subsequent terms we can see here that it is able to reference those new tabs, pull in information, and script the respective actions to understand what actually has to be done.
zh: 然后在随后的术语中我们可以在这里看到它能够引用那些新标签页,拉入信息,并编写相应动作来理解实际上必须做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that speeds up these actions significantly because Codex in browser use can actually look at, for example, one page, understand the structure, and then write a script to perform like scraping, for example, on subsequent pages more easily.
zh: 所以这显著加速了这些动作,因为在浏览器使用中的 Codex 实际上可以看,例如,一页,理解结构,然后编写一个脚本来执行像抓取,例如,在随后的页面上更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third thing is file system interactions.
zh: 第三件事是文件系统交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you're using Codex or any coding agent, of course, you want it to be able to interact with the file system.
zh: 我认为如果你正在使用 Codex 或任何编码智能体,当然,你希望它能够与文件系统交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the case of our models, all of the recent models starting with GPT-5 have been trained on the concept of an apply patch tool to do file editing, which means that they're used to using that to change files by giving it a diff and then also using that same thing to create new files.
zh: 在我们的模型的情况下,所有最近的模型从 GPT-5 开始都被训练了应用补丁工具的概念来做文件编辑,这意味着它们习惯使用它来通过给它一个差异来改变文件,然后也使用同样的东西来创建新文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for everything else, it uses a shell tool where it will do file search or other file system navigation.
zh: 然后对于其他一切,它使用一个 shell 工具,它将在那里做文件搜索或其他文件系统导航。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will see the model naturally trying to use ripgrap since that's what it got used to during training.
zh: 你将看到模型自然地尝试使用 ripgrap,因为那是它在训练期间习惯的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're actually in the Codex harness shipping ripgrap with the harness if you don't have it installed on your own.
zh: 所以我们实际上在 Codex 挽具中随挽具一起提供 ripgrap,如果你自己没有安装它。

speaker: Unknown
en: On Windows, we also trained the model to use PowerShell natively.
zh: 在 Windows 上,我们还训练模型原生使用 PowerShell。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we were running it on Windows, you will see it start writing PowerShell code instead.
zh: 所以如果我们在 Windows 上运行它,你将看到它开始编写 PowerShell 代码代替。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things you're seeing here is the sandbox pulling in.
zh: 你在这里看到的一件事是沙箱拉入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all of the interactions that you see with the file system actually go through our sandbox layer.
zh: 所以你看到的与文件系统的所有交互实际上都通过我们的沙箱层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on Mac OS, we use Seatbelt for that, similar to most agents.
zh: 在 Mac OS 上,我们为此使用 Seatbelt,类似于大多数智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on Linux, we use Bubblewrap.
zh: 在 Linux 上,我们使用 Bubblewrap。

speaker: Unknown
en: On Windows, it's slightly different, where we actually had to build our own custom open source Windows sandbox.
zh: 在 Windows 上,它略有不同,我们实际上必须构建我们自己的自定义开源 Windows 沙箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in the same GitHub repository, if you want to take a look.
zh: 它在同一个 GitHub 仓库中,如果你想看一看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's many reasons why we had to do this, and I could probably fill a whole talk about that.
zh: 我们必须这样做有很多原因,我可能会为此填满整个演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead, I would recommend you to actually check out the article that
zh: 所以相反,我会推荐你实际上去看看那篇文章

speaker: Unknown
en: David wrote about this.
zh: David 写了关于这个的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It goes into all of the other Windows alternatives and why we actually had to build our own sandbox there.
zh: 它会深入所有其他的 Windows 替代方案，以及为什么我们实际上不得不在那里构建我们自己的沙箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Highly fascinating if you really want to nerd out about Windows internals.
zh: 如果你真的想深入钻研 Windows 内部机制，这是高度引人入胜的。

speaker: Unknown
en: With sandboxes, though, one of the biggest complaints is always approval fatigue.
zh: 然而，对于沙箱，最大的抱怨之一始终是审批疲劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many of you get annoyed by approvals, especially for long tasks and have run in full access?
zh: 你们中有多少人会对审批感到恼火，特别是对于长时间的任务，并且已经开启了完全访问权限？

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think the audience gets filmed, so we're going to do this again.
